questions.question: What is the difference between functional and class components in React?
questions.title: Functional vs Class Components in React — Differences & Migration
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between functional and class components in React?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Stateless vs stateful (pre-hooks), hooks replaced class lifecycle, function components are the modern default, performance parity.

**Classic weak answer:** Believing class components are faster than function components — they're not; function components are the recommended default since hooks (React 16.8+).

**Senior finish:** Mention React has deprecated some class-only APIs (class-based error boundaries remain); new APIs (Suspense-for-data, Server Components) are function-only.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Functional vs Class Components in React — Differences & Migration** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the difference between functional and class components in React?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Stateless vs stateful (pre-hooks), hooks replaced class lifecycle, function components are the modern default, performance parity**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Believing class components are faster than function components — they're not; function components are the recommended default since hooks (React 16.8+)**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention React has deprecated some class-only APIs (class-based error boundaries remain); new APIs (Suspense-for-data, Server Components) are function-only**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Stateless vs stateful (pre-hooks), hooks replaced class lifecycle, function components are the modern default, performance parity
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **believing class components are faster than function components — they're not; function components are the recommended default since hooks (React 16.8+)** and what you do instead.

questions.question: What is JSX? How does it transpile to JavaScript?
questions.title: What Is JSX in React? — How It Compiles to React.createElement
questions.direct_answer:
What is JSX? How does it transpile to JavaScript?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** JSX is syntactic sugar over React.createElement (or jsx() in the new transform), Babel/SWC transpiles it, attributes become props, children are variadic.

**Classic weak answer:** Thinking JSX must return a single parent — Fragments (<> </>) allow multiple roots without a wrapper div.

**Senior finish:** Mention the new JSX transform (React 17+) removes the need to import React in scope; tie into server components.
